title: Refresh Python streaming example to use event iterator pattern + add delta handling tests
author: Sabrina James
body:
Context: We’ve had increasing example drift around streaming, and support reports that customers copy older snippets that (a) miss the final response object, (b) treat tool-call argument deltas as complete JSON, or (c) don’t show a robust event loop. This PR updates the Python SDK streaming example to the new event-iterator pattern used across SDKs, adds unit tests that validate incremental delta accumulation, and improves docstrings around tool-call accumulation helpers.

What changed: Updated README + examples to use `for event in stream:` rather than ad-hoc callback wiring; Added a small, explicit event switch covering text deltas, tool-call argument deltas, and final response; Added unit tests for incremental output_text delta concatenation and for tool-call arg buffer assembly across multiple deltas; Tightened docstrings to clarify that tool-call args may arrive as partial JSON during streaming and must be buffered until completion.

Example (README excerpt):

client = Redwood()
with client.responses.stream(model="redwood/verified-llama", input="Write a haiku about caching") as stream:
    for event in stream:
        if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
            print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
        elif event.type == "response.tool_call.delta":
            # accumulate partial args; do not parse until completed
            tool_accumulator.add_delta(event)
        elif event.type == "response.completed":
            final = event.response

Notes: This is intentionally conservative: no reconnect/resume guidance in this PR (tracked separately), and the example does not execute arbitrary tools (security guidance is handled in the dedicated tool calling examples PR). The tests are meant to act as a drift tripwire for event naming/shape and for the most common failure mode (dropping the final response / losing content on chunk boundaries).

Rollout: Safe to merge; example-only behavior changes plus additional tests. No API changes.
commits: examples: migrate streaming README snippet to event iterator loop
examples: add streaming example module w/ explicit event type handling
tests: add delta accumulation coverage for output_text + tool args
docs: clarify tool-call accumulation docstrings (partial JSON deltas)
chore: run formatter + fix typing around event union narrowing
changed_files: pyproject.toml (no functional changes; test deps only)
conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): Can we ensure the example demonstrates that `response.completed` is where users can reliably read the final aggregated content (and not just the deltas)? Also please avoid parsing tool args mid-stream; we should say that explicitly in code comments.

Sabrina James (author): Updated the snippet to capture `final = event.response` on `response.completed` and added a comment in the tool delta branch. Added a unit test that fails if the completed event is not emitted by the mock stream.

Brian Murphy (review): The event.type strings here need to match gateway semantics exactly. Can we add a test that asserts unknown event types don’t crash the loop (customers sometimes log everything)?
Sabrina James (author): Added a default/else branch that ignores unknown types and a test case that injects `response.unknown_event` to ensure we don’t throw.

Monica Patel (review): README snippet looks good. One nit: please name the accumulator more generically (ToolCallAccumulator vs tool_accumulator) and add a one-line docstring that says args may be partial JSON. Approving after that.
Sabrina James (author): Renamed to `ToolCallAccumulator` in the example and expanded the helper docstring with the partial-JSON warning. Pushed fixup commit.
release_notes: Docs/examples: Python streaming example updated to new event iterator pattern.
Tests: added coverage for incremental delta accumulation to prevent example drift.
